sections.title: Introduction
sections.text: Optrans TMS is a transportation management system that helps businesses standardize master data, coordinate operations, control freight charges, and calculate driver salaries on one platform. Use this page to find the guidance that matches the task you need to complete. English documentation is currently available for System Account Management; links marked Vietnamese only open the corresponding Vietnamese guides. Start by task - Administer the system: start with user accounts and partner data ( Vietnamese only ). - Coordinate transportation operations: review a typical operating workflow ( Vietnamese only ) or go directly to Booking/Order management ( Vietnamese only ). - Manage freight charges: configure freight rates ( Vietnamese only ), then calculate order charges ( Vietnamese only ). - Manage driver payroll: configure salary norms ( Vietnamese only ), then process trip salary ( Vietnamese only ). Modules covered by this manual System Account Management Create and manage accounts for drivers and dispatchers, including password changes, phone-number updates, account deactivation, and deletion. Start with creating a driver account or creating a dispatcher account . Master Data Management Maintain shared transportation data, including partners, drivers, locations, routes, cargo, vehicles, and related catalogs. Start with customer information ( Vietnamese only ) or location management ( Vietnamese only ). Operations Follow the process from Bookings/Orders, Containers/Waybills, driver tasks, and dispatch orders through expenses, documents, and reports. Start with a typical operating workflow ( Vietnamese only ) or the Booking/Order management menu ( Vietnamese only ). Fee Management Configure freight rates, route groups, and fee items; load data, calculate charges, and confirm charges for orders or waybills. Start with freight rates ( Vietnamese only ) or order charges ( Vietnamese only ). Driver Salary Management Configure salary norms and structures, maintain related cost rules, and calculate salaries by trip or by month. Start with salary norms ( Vietnamese only ) or trip salary ( Vietnamese only ). Typical workflow 1. Create user accounts and prepare master data. 2. Receive orders, manage waybills, and coordinate execution. 3. Load data, calculate freight charges, and confirm the results. 4. Calculate driver salaries and monitor results through operations reports. This sequence is an orientation guide. Open each module for detailed prerequisites and procedures. How to use this manual - Use the sidebar to open a module and select a guide. - Use the table of contents on the right to jump to a section on the current page. - Use the language selector at the top of the page to switch between Vietnamese and English.

sections.title: Create a driver account
sections.text: Steps Step 1 Go to the Account module → open the Users menu → click the New button Step 2 Enter the login information Name: enter the driver's name Email Address: enter the driver's phone number (this is the phone number the driver uses to sign in to the mobile app) User Group: defaults to "Container" Is Driver: check this field if this is a driver account Step 3 Click Add a line → find and select the "Driver" role Step 4 Click the Save button, or press CTRL + S, or click the manual-save indicator to finish creating the account. Step 5 Set an initial password for the account Click the action button → select "Change Password": The change-password popup appears → enter the new password in the " New Password " field and click CHANGE PASSWORD → The driver account has been created. The driver will sign in to the mobile app using this phone number and the password just set. Step 6 The user administrator notifies the dispatch department that the driver account has been created. The dispatcher then goes to the system, opens the Driver menu, and fills in the driver's personal information.

sections.title: Create a dispatcher account
sections.text: Steps Step 1 Go to the Settings module → open the Users menu → click the New button Step 2 Enter the login information Name: enter the dispatcher's name Email Address: enter the dispatcher's company email User Group: defaults to "Container" Is Driver: do NOT check this field Step 3 Click Add a line → find and select the " Dispatcher " role Step 4 Click the Save button, or press CTRL + S, to finish creating the account. Step 5 Set an initial password for the account Click the action button → select "Change Password": The change-password popup appears → enter the new password in the " New Password " field and click CHANGE PASSWORD → The dispatcher account has been created.

sections.title: Driver changes phone number
sections.text: Steps Step 1 Go to the Account module → open the Users menu → click the driver account whose phone number needs to change Step 2 Enter the new phone number in the Email Address field Step 3 Click SAVE, or press CTRL + S, to finish

sections.title: Change account password
sections.text: Steps Step 1 Open the account whose password needs to change → click the action button → Change Password The change-password popup appears → enter the new password in the " New Password " field and click CHANGE PASSWORD

sections.title: Archive an account
sections.text: For accounts that are no longer used — for example a driver or dispatcher who has left the company — the account should be archived. Steps Step 1 Open the account to archive → click the icon → click "Archive" Step 2 The system asks for confirmation → if you're sure, click ARCHIVE

sections.title: Delete an account
sections.text: Use this when an account needs to be deleted — for example, a duplicate or a mistakenly created account. Steps Step 1 Open the account to delete → click the icon → click "Delete" Step 2 The system asks for confirmation → click OK to confirm

sections.title: Salary standards overview
sections.text: Purpose Salary standards are used to declare the salary rate for each transport route. The rate can differ by area, order type, container size and customer. Access Menu: Driver salary Configuration Salary standards

sections.title: Creating a salary standard
sections.text: Step 1 Click New . Step 2 Enter the general information, and the conditions for the customer and the route. Field Meaning Item Salary item that applies. Effective date Date the standard starts applying; you can also declare an end date. Value The salary rate. Company Company the standard applies to. Customer Customer the standard applies to specifically, if any. Order type Order type it applies to, such as Export container, Import container or Warehouse transfer. Container size Container size it applies to, such as 20ft, 40ft or Bulk cargo. Route group Transport route it applies to. From location / To location Location range of the route it applies to. Step 3 Click Save manually to save the standard.

sections.title: Editing a salary standard
sections.text: Step 1 Select the standard you want to edit from the list. Step 2 Change the information you need, then click Save manually .

sections.title: Deleting a salary standard
sections.text: Step 1 Select the record you want to delete. Step 2 Select Actions Delete . Step 3 Confirm with the Delete button. This removes the record permanently.

sections.title: Salary structures overview
sections.text: Purpose A salary structure defines the components of a driver's salary and how it is calculated. A structure can only be used for calculation when it is Approved . Access Menu: Driver salary Salary structures Types of salary structure The system has two types of structure: - Dispatch Salary : the trip salary structure. - Monthly Salary : the monthly salary structure. Choose the correct Structure Type before configuring the salary components.

sections.title: Creating a salary structure
sections.text: Step 1 Click New . Step 2 Enter the general information and choose the Structure Type . Field Meaning Name Name of the salary structure. Code Generated by the system or entered manually. Driver Leave empty to apply to all drivers; select a driver to apply to that driver only. Structure Type Choose Dispatch Salary or Monthly Salary . Effective date Date the structure starts applying. Description Additional notes, if any. Step 3 On the relevant component tab, click Add a line . Step 4 Declare the salary component on the trip salary creation screen. Field Meaning Item Select the item, for example Transport distance, Trip salary or Vehicle standby. Items are declared under Salary items . Code Code of the item. Type Choose Parameter or Formula . Effective date Period during which the component applies. Value based on System data used as the input. Fixed value Fixed value or amount that applies. Input data Data used to calculate the component. Formula Formula for calculating the salary, when the type is Formula. Step 5 Choose one of these ways to save the component line: - Save & Close : create one data line and close the screen. - Save & New : create one data line and keep the screen open to create another. Step 6 Click Save manually to save the salary structure. A new structure is only in the Draft state. Without salary components, the system cannot calculate a salary. When calculating a salary from a structure, the system uses the salary standard that matches the applicable conditions.

sections.title: Approving a salary structure
sections.text: The structure lifecycle is Draft → Waiting for approval → Approved . A Draft structure is not applied yet, one Waiting for approval is awaiting confirmation, and an Approved one is used to calculate salaries. Step 1 In the Draft state, click Confirm to move the structure to Waiting for approval. Step 2 In the Waiting for approval state, click Approve . Step 3 Confirm the approval. The structure moves to the Approved state and can be used to calculate salaries.

sections.title: Canceling a salary structure
sections.text: Step 1 Click Cancel . Step 2 Confirm with the OK button. The structure then moves to the Canceled state.

sections.title: Editing and re-approving
sections.text: A structure cannot be edited while it is Waiting for approval , Approved or Canceled . Any change must be returned to Draft and approved again before it applies. Step 1 Select the structure you want to edit. Step 2 Click Reset to draft to return the structure to the Draft state. Step 3 Confirm with the OK button. Step 4 Change the information you need. Step 5 Click Save manually . Step 6 Run the Confirm and then Approve process again so the structure returns to the Approved state.

sections.text: Purpose Distance standards declare the standard distance for each route so you can control the operating mileage, calculate salary per kilometre or per route, compare against actual GPS data, and set the allowed margin of error. Access Menu: Driver salary Distance standards

sections.title: Creating a distance standard

Route Transport route it applies to. Standard distance (km) Standard number of kilometres for the route. Maximum distance (km) Maximum number of kilometres allowed; this is a limit, not the standard distance. % Buffer Percentage by which the standard distance may be exceeded. Effective date Date the standard starts applying. Company Company the data applies to. Step 3 Fill in the required fields: name, location, effective date, standard distance and company. Step 4 Click Save manually . The new distance standard appears in the list. sections.title: How it works
sections.text: When a waybill is created, the system automatically creates the matching trip salary record. To calculate the salary, the record must have both a matching salary standard and a matching salary structure . The structure used must be Approved ; if either configuration is missing, the system cannot calculate the salary. When no standard is selected manually, the system finds the matching standard by transport route, area, order type, container size and customer. If the user selects a standard manually, that standard takes priority over the automatic result. Accessing and viewing the list Step 1 Go to the Driver salary Trip salary menu. The list screen shows the trip salary records that need handling. Step 2 To change which fields the list shows, click the column configuration icon. Select or clear the columns you want to follow, then apply the configuration.

sections.title: Calculating and confirming trip salary
sections.text: Step 1 Select the trip salary row you want to calculate to open its details. Step 2 Check the Salary structure and the Salary standard . If either is missing, or you want to replace the automatic standard, select the structure and/or the standard you need. When you select a standard manually, that standard takes priority for the current calculation. Step 3 Click Save manually to save the structure and standard you selected. Step 4 Click Load data to load the input data for the calculation. Once it has loaded, check the data on the Trip salary tab. Step 5 Click Calculate . When the calculation succeeds, the salary status changes to OK and the total salary is updated. Step 6 Click Confirm to approve the trip salary record, then confirm in the dialog if the system asks. A confirmed record can be used in the monthly salary process. Notes on handling errors Do not confirm a record before checking that its status is OK . A trip salary record that has an error or is unconfirmed leaves the monthly salary result incomplete. When you hit an error, check the approved structure, the matching conditions of the standard and the input data, then select a standard manually if needed, save, reload the data and recalculate. Related links - Salary standards - Salary structures - Monthly salary

Before calculating, handle the trip salary records so that they are OK and Confirmed . The related configurations are salary standards , salary structures and, where it applies, monthly default salary . Note: A trip with an error or one that is unconfirmed does not produce a clean monthly salary result. Handle those trips before closing and recalculating the monthly salary.

In that example, 4 trips need recalculating and 23 trips are not yet OK or not yet confirmed. Step 3 Switch to the Trip salary tab to manage the driver's dispatch orders and check the status of each trip. Step 4 For a row with an error, open it to see the details, select the matching Salary standard , then click Calculate to recalculate. Once the status is OK , click Save to finish handling that row. Repeat for the remaining rows with errors.

Step 2 Once the valid rows are OK , select Confirm to confirm them in bulk. Step 3 Click Calculate for the driver's monthly payslip to complete the monthly consolidation. The result shows the total salary the driver receives for the month. Related links - Trip salary - Salary standards - Salary structures - Monthly default salary

Form for the general information and applicable conditions of a freight rate Field Meaning Charge item Identifies the type of charge or fee being declared in the system. Freight rate Name of the main charge item used to calculate the transport amount for an order or a waybill. Effective date Date from which the freight rate applies. The system only uses the rate table when the transport date falls within the effective period. End date Date on which the rate stops applying. If left empty, the system treats the rate as valid indefinitely. Unit price (-V) Main rate applied to the corresponding transport route, used to calculate the total freight amount. Created on Date the rate record was created in the system. Created by User who declared or created the freight rate. Source Data source or origin of the freight rate, if the system maps data automatically. Description Additional notes about the scope or content of the rate table. Customer Customer the rate applies to; the system maps the rate by customer on the order or waybill. Order type Transport type the rate table applies to, for example Export container, Import container, Warehouse transfer or Bulk cargo. Container size Condition based on container size, such as 20ft, 40ft or Bulk cargo. Route group Main transport route the rate applies to; the system uses the route group to find the rate table automatically. From location Origin of the transport route. To location Destination of the transport route. Cargo type Cargo group the rate table applies to, for example refrigerated cargo, dangerous goods or bulk cargo. sections.title: Booking and order management menu
sections.text: - Bookings : this menu contains every booking and order. - Booking documents : this menu contains every document of the bookings and orders.

sections.title: Creating a booking or order
sections.text: Note A booking sent by a customer normally becomes one booking or order in the system. In some cases, though, one customer booking has to be split into several bookings or orders in the system. The dispatcher can split it as needed. Creating a new booking or order Step 1 Go to a booking or order menu → click New . Step 2 Enter the main information of the order. Field Description Booking code Enter the booking number or the reference order number. Order code Leave this empty; the system generates it. Customer Select the customer. Type a name or a phone number to search. Tracking code Leave this empty; the system generates it. Person in charge Select the person in charge of the booking on the customer side. Internal person in charge The person in charge of this booking inside your company. The system defaults to whoever created the booking; you can change it. Order type Select an order type. The order type decides what other information the system shows — order documents, the default task list, and so on. The order types are: - Export a full container: - For a full container export booking. - Default tasks: pick up empty container, drop off empty container, pick up laden container, deliver laden container. - Import a full container: - For a full container import booking. - Default tasks: pick up laden container, deliver laden container, pick up empty container, return empty container. - Move an empty container: - For moving a container between ports or depots. - Default tasks: pick up empty container, drop off empty container. - Move a laden container: - For moving a laden container between domestic ports or depots. - Default tasks: pick up laden container, deliver laden container. - Bulk cargo: - For carrying cargo on a flatbed or skeletal trailer. - Default tasks: pick up cargo, deliver cargo. Booking note Enter a note for the booking or order — for example the list of places where an empty container can be picked up. Step 3 Enter the order size, which is the number of containers the customer has asked you to carry for this booking. - The system loads this table when you select the Order type . Enter the number of containers of each type in the Quantity column. Step 4 Attach the documents of the order. Field Description Document type When you select the Order type , the system loads this list from what has been configured. Share with the driver Lets you share the document attached to the order so the driver has everything they need while working. Description Add details for each document. Attachment Click ATTACH DOCUMENT to upload files from your computer. Hard copy status Two values: - No hard copy - Hard copy received If the customer has already given you the hard copy of that document, set it to "Hard copy received" to record that. If you need documents beyond the default list, click "Add a line" to add another document type to the order. Step 5 Enter the transport plan. Field Description Empty container delivery deadline Enter the time the customer wants the empty container delivered to their warehouse. Applies to full container export orders. SI Cutoff Enter the SI Cutoff time. Applies to full container export orders. Port Cutoff Enter the SI/CY Cutoff time. Applies to full container export orders. Laden container delivery date Enter the time the customer wants the laden container delivered to their warehouse. Applies to full container import orders. DEM date Enter the DEM time. Applies to full container import orders. DET date Enter the DET time. Applies to full container import orders. Order task list table Depending on the order type you selected, the system loads the default task list already configured. This is the route of tasks the driver has to follow. You also need to fill in the location, planned date and deadline columns. Step 6 Click SAVE , or press CTRL + S , to save the order. The system records who created the order and when on the [Other information] tab:

sections.title: Confirming a booking or order
sections.text: There are two ways to confirm a booking or order - Option 1: confirm one specific booking or order. - Option 2: confirm many bookings or orders at once. Option 1 Confirming one specific booking or order - Step 1: on the details screen of an order → click CONFIRM . When you confirm, the system checks whether all the required documents are attached and whether the task route table is filled in. - If the system warns you, complete the missing information and confirm again. - Step 2: a successfully confirmed order shows the message below. Click CLOSE , or press ESC , to dismiss it. The order then moves to the CONFIRMED state. Option 2 Confirming many bookings or orders at once - Step 1: open the booking or order list → tick the bookings and orders you want to confirm. - Step 2: click CONFIRM . When you confirm, the system checks whether all the required documents are attached and whether the task route table is filled in for each order. If the system warns you, complete the missing information and confirm again. - Step 3: a successfully confirmed order shows the message below. Click CLOSE , or press ESC , to dismiss it. The order then moves to the CONFIRMED state.

sections.title: Canceling a booking or order
sections.text: Note You can only cancel an order while it is NEW or CONFIRMED . Canceling an order Step 1 Open the order you want to cancel → click CANCEL . Step 2 The system asks "Are you sure you want to cancel the order?" → if you are, click OK . Step 3 The order has been canceled and moves to the CANCELED state, as below.

sections.title: Deleting a booking or order
sections.text: Note You can only delete an order while it is NEW or CANCELED . Deleting an order Step 1 Open the order you want to delete, or open the order list and tick the orders you want to delete → click the action icon (the cog) → click the delete action, as below. Step 2 The system asks you to confirm that you want to delete the data. If you are sure, click OK.

sections.title: The states of a booking or order
sections.text: A booking or order has the following states: 1. New: the order has just been created. 2. Confirmed: the order has been confirmed successfully. 3. Waybill: containers and waybills have been created for the order and they are not complete yet. 4. Completed: every container and waybill of the order is complete. 5. Canceled: the order has been canceled, or every container and waybill of the order has been canceled.

sections.title: Viewing the planned date of an order
sections.text: By default the system sorts orders by planned date, newest first. The timeline columns: the system collects the important dates of an order in these columns. If you need specific date columns for sorting or for a closer look, click the icon at the end of the header and turn on the fields you want:

sections.title: The overdue status of a booking or order
sections.text: The overdue statuses of an order 1. Overdue: past the deadline. 2. Due soon: within 6 hours of the deadline. 3. Normal: more than 6 hours before the deadline. How the system works out whether an order is overdue ( ) For orders that already have containers and waybills: 1. An "Overdue" order: a. When any waybill is incomplete and that waybill is "Overdue". b. A waybill is "Overdue" when one of its tasks is "Overdue" and that task is not complete. 2. A "Due soon" order: a. When any waybill is incomplete and that waybill is "Due soon". b. A waybill is "Due soon" when one of its tasks is "Due soon" and that task is not complete. 3. A "Normal" order: a. When every waybill is "Normal". b. A waybill is "Normal" when every one of its tasks is "Normal". ( ) For orders with no waybill yet, the system uses the deadline on the order's task table: 1. An "Overdue" order: a. When any task is "Overdue". 2. A "Due soon" order: a. When any task is "Due soon". 3. A "Normal" order: a. When every task is "Normal". Viewing the overdue status In the booking and order list The system shows a light column so you can tell the overdue status of an order at a glance. - Overdue: red light - Due soon: yellow light - Normal: green light On the details screen of a booking or order When an order is "Due soon" or "Overdue", the system shows a matching ribbon as below. The system also provides the "Overdue" and "Due soon" filters and a grouping by "Overdue status" so you can filter the data easily:

sections.title: Viewing container status from a booking or order
sections.text: There are two ways to see the status of the containers in an order: - From the order list - On the details screen of an order From the order list You can check the waybill status of an order at a glance, as below: - The Waybill status column: the system shows the number of containers and waybills per status. - Created: the total number of containers created for the order. - To create: from the number of containers you entered in the order size table and the number already created, the system works out how many are left to create. - Confirmed: the number of containers in the "Confirmed" state. - Assigned: the number of containers in the "Assigned" state. - In progress: the number of containers in the "In progress" state. - Completed: the number of containers in the "Completed" state. - Not completed: the number of containers in the "Not completed" state. - Canceled: the number of containers in the "Canceled" state. On the order details screen You can also see the waybill status and the waybill list of an order on the [Container/Waybill] tab (1), or by clicking the Waybill link button (2), as below.

sections.title: Container and waybill management menu
sections.text: - Waybills: this menu contains every container and waybill of every order. - Waybill documents: this menu contains every document of the waybills.

sections.title: Creating the containers and waybills for a booking
sections.text: Creating waybills Step 1 Open the booking — it has to be confirmed — → click CREATE WAYBILL . The system uses the number of containers in the booking's order size table and creates the matching waybills automatically: Step 2 The system returns the list of containers and waybills it has just created. - Every container and waybill created is in the NEW state. - These containers and waybills are still missing data, so they are highlighted in red. Once all the required fields are filled in, the red highlight goes away.

sections.title: Filling in each container and waybill
sections.text: Ways to fill in waybill information - Option 1: fill in each waybill one at a time. - Option 2: use "Mass Edit" to update many waybills at once. Option 1: one waybill at a time - Step 1: open each waybill and enter the order and waybill information: Field Description Container number Enter the container number for the "Import a full container" and "Move a laden container domestically" order types. For the "Export a full container" order type, the driver enters the container number in the mobile app and the system synchronises it back to TMS. The dispatcher can also enter it for them. Waybill code Leave this empty; the system generates it. Customer Leave this empty; the system takes it from the order. Booking/Order Leave this empty; the system takes it from the order. Booking code Leave this empty; the system takes it from the order. Order type Leave this empty; the system takes it from the order. Booking note Leave this empty; the system takes it from the order. You can change it. Planned date Leave this empty; the system takes it from the order. You can change it. Container size Leave this empty; the system selects it when the waybill is created from the order. You can change it. Container type Enter or search for the container type in the list. Seal number Enter the seal number for the "Import a full container" order type. For "Export a full container", the driver enters it in the mobile app and the data is synchronised back to TMS. Container pickup code Enter the pickup code as a note for the driver collecting the container. Container pickup place Leave this empty; the system takes it from the order. Stuffing/unstuffing place Leave this empty; the system takes it from the order. Container drop-off place Leave this empty; the system takes it from the order. Container delivery date Leave this empty; the system takes it from the order. You can update it. DEM / CY Cutoff date The system shows either DEM or CY Cutoff depending on the order type. Leave this empty; the system takes it from the order. You can update it. DET / SI Cutoff date The system shows either DET or SI Cutoff depending on the order type. Leave this empty; the system takes it from the order. You can update it. Planned driver Select or search for the driver assigned to carry this container. Planned vehicle Select or search for the vehicle assigned to carry this container. Planned trailer Select or search for the trailer assigned to carry this container. Carrier Select or search for the carrier in charge, if a third party is carrying it for you. Note for the carrier Enter a note for the carrier taking the waybill — for example the PIN for collecting the laden container. - Step 2: enter the waybill notes: Field Description Customer note Enter the customer's note for the container, if any. Waybill note Enter a note for the container or waybill, if any. Note for the driver Enter a note for the driver, if any — for example container requirements or the pickup time. Freight note Enter a note from the freight team about additional costs or other matters, if any. - Step 3: enter the cargo and customs declaration information: Field Description Cargo Select the type of cargo. Packaging Select the packaging specification for the cargo. VGM Enter the VGM. Declaration number Enter the customs declaration number. Customs channel Select the customs channel. Customs cleared Tick this once customs has been cleared. - Step 4: enter the port and container transfer information, if any: Field Description Port of loading Leave this empty; the system takes it from the order for reference. Transshipment port Leave this empty; the system takes it from the order for reference. Port of destination Leave this empty; the system takes it from the order for reference. Container transfer option The system takes the default from the order, but you can adjust it for each container and waybill. Container transfer status Three values: Not started (the default), In progress, Completed. While the container is being transferred between ports, you can update this to keep track. Container transfer note Enter a note about the transfer, if any. - Step 5: fill in the tasks of the waybill. This task table is created from the template task table on the order. - On the task table of each waybill you can: - Click "Add a line" to add a task. - Click the "Bin" icon at the end of a row to delete that task. - Click any row to see the details of that task. - Click the icon and drag to reorder the tasks. - Enter the task information: Field Description Task code The system generates this. Leave it empty. Task Name of the task. Task status How far along the task is. It changes as the driver works or the dispatcher updates it. Location Where the task is carried out. Contact The contact at that location. Mobile The contact's phone number. Note for the driver A note for the driver, if any. It is shown in the mobile app. Planned date Enter the date you plan the driver to carry out the task. The dispatcher sets a date that makes dispatching work well. Deadline Enter the deadline from the paperwork, or one the dispatcher sets to keep track of the task. Plan The container plan at the customer's warehouse. Applies to tasks such as "Deliver laden container" or "Drop off empty container" at a customer warehouse. The values are: drop container, detach trailer, store vehicle. This is also shown in the mobile app so the driver knows the plan. Whether this field appears depends on the configuration. - Step 6: click SAVE , or press CTRL + S , to save.

sections.title: Using \"Mass Edit\" to update many at once
sections.text: Ways to fill in waybill information - Option 1: fill in each waybill one at a time. - Option 2: use "Mass Edit" to update many waybills at once. Option 2: Mass Edit — updating many at once Step 1 On the container and waybill list, tick the waybills you want to update in bulk (1) → click Actions (2) → click the "Mass Edit" entry for that order type (3). Step 2 The system shows the popup below. Enter values for the fields you want to change: 1. Fields to change: choose Set and enter the value next to it. 2. Fields to leave alone: leave them on Don't touch. Step 3 Click APPLY on the popup to update them all. Note The system only lets you select waybills that belong to the same order for a bulk update.

sections.title: Quickly filling in container and seal numbers
sections.text: For an "Export a full container" waybill, the driver enters the container and seal numbers in the mobile app when they complete the "Pick up empty container" task, and both are synchronised from the mobile app to Odoo. For an "Import a full container" waybill, the dispatcher has to fill both in after the waybill is created. Here is how to do that quickly from the waybill list, without opening each waybill: Step 1 On the container and waybill list, tick the waybills whose container and seal numbers you want to update (1) → click Actions (2) → click the "Enter container & seal numbers in bulk" entry for that order type (3). Step 2 The system shows the popup below. Click each "Container number" and "Seal number" cell of each waybill to fill it in. Step 3 Click Save to store the container and seal numbers you entered.

sections.title: Confirming a container or waybill
sections.text: Ways to confirm a container or waybill - Option 1: confirm one specific container or waybill. - Option 2: confirm many containers or waybills at once. Option 1: Confirming one specific container or waybill Step 1 On the details screen of a waybill → click CONFIRM . When you confirm, the system checks whether the waybill has all the information it needs. If the system warns you, complete the missing information and confirm again. Step 2: A successfully confirmed waybill shows the message below. Click CLOSE , or press ESC , to dismiss it. The waybill then moves to the CONFIRMED state. Option 2: Confirming many containers or waybills at once Step 1 Open the container and waybill list → tick the containers and waybills you want to confirm. Step 2 Click CONFIRM . When you confirm, the system checks whether each waybill has all the information it needs. If the system warns you, complete the missing information and confirm again. Step 3 A successfully confirmed waybill shows the message below. Click CLOSE , or press ESC , to dismiss it. The waybill then moves to the CONFIRMED state.

sections.title: Creating a dispatch order for a container or waybill
sections.text: Steps Step 1 Open the waybill list → tick the waybill you want to dispatch → click DISPATCH . Note: One dispatch order can take either one 40ft waybill, or one 20ft waybill, or two 20ft waybills as a container pair. Step 2 The system shows the dispatch planning screen as below. The image below shows the waybills selected for dispatch planning. - You can choose the dispatch date in the "Dispatch date" box to assign the orders to the same day. - The list shows a summary for each container — order details, locations, container number and so on — so the dispatcher can plan properly. - Click the "X" on a row to remove that container or waybill from the plan. - Click "Add a line" to open the waybill search popup and add another waybill to the plan. Fill in each row of the plan to assign a driver and a vehicle to the waybill: - Planned driver : select the driver being assigned. - Planned vehicle : when you select the driver, the system fills in that driver's default vehicle. You can still choose another one. - Planned trailer : when you select the driver, the system fills in the default trailer for that driver's vehicle. You can still choose another one. - Planned date : the system takes it from the planned date of the selected waybills. You can change it. - Container number: the system takes it from the container number of the selected waybills. You can change it. - Container size: the system takes it from the container size of the selected waybills. You can change it. Step 3 Once everything is filled in, click CREATE AND SEND TO DRIVER . - The system creates a new dispatch order and sends it to the driver.

sections.title: Canceling a container or waybill
sections.text: Note You can only cancel a container or waybill while it is not complete. There are two kinds of cancellation: - Cancelled internally - Cancelled by the customer. Canceling a container or waybill Step 1 Open the waybill you want to cancel → click CANCEL . Step 2 The system asks "Are you sure you want to cancel the waybill?" → if you are, click OK . Step 3 The system shows the cancellation popup as below → select the cancellation type and enter the reason → click OK . - Read the notes highlighted in red before you confirm the cancellation. Step 4 The system changes the state of the waybill. - For cancellation type = Cancelled internally: the system moves the waybill to CANCELED . - For cancellation type = Cancelled by the customer: the system moves the waybill to NOT COMPLETED . - Keeping the two kinds of cancellation in separate states makes it easy to tell them apart when charging the customer, if that applies.

sections.title: Deleting a container or waybill
sections.text: Note You can only delete a waybill while it is NEW or CANCELED . Deleting a waybill Step 1 Open the waybill you want to delete, or open the waybill list and tick the waybills you want to delete → click the action icon (the cog) → click the delete action, as below. Step 2 The system asks you to confirm that you want to delete the data. If you are sure, click OK.

sections.title: The states of a container or waybill
sections.text: A container or waybill has the following states: 1. New: the waybill has just been created. 2. Confirmed: the waybill has been confirmed successfully. 3. Assigned: the waybill has been assigned to a dispatch order. As soon as any one task of the waybill is dispatched, the waybill moves to assigned. 4. In progress: any one task of the waybill has been started. 5. Completed: every task of the waybill is complete. 6. Not completed: the waybill was cancelled with the type "cancelled by the customer". 6. Canceled: the waybill was cancelled with the type "cancelled internally", or every task of the waybill was cancelled.

sections.title: Viewing the planned date
sections.text: By default the system sorts containers and waybills by planned date, newest first. - The "Planned start" column: the system takes the planned date of the first task in that waybill. - The "Planned end" column: the system takes the planned date of the last task in that waybill. - The Timeline columns: the system collects the important dates of the waybill in these columns. If you need specific date columns for sorting or for a closer look, click the icon at the end of the header and turn on the fields you want:

sections.title: The overdue status
sections.text: The overdue statuses of a container or waybill 1. Overdue: past the deadline. 2. Due soon: within 6 hours of the deadline. 3. Normal: more than 6 hours before the deadline. How the system works out whether a container or waybill is overdue 1. An "Overdue" waybill: when one of its tasks is "Overdue" and that task is not complete. 2. A "Due soon" waybill: when one of its tasks is "Due soon" and that task is not complete. 3. A "Normal" waybill: when every task of the waybill is "Normal". Viewing the overdue status In the container and waybill list The system shows a light column so you can tell the overdue status of a waybill at a glance. - Overdue: red light - Due soon: yellow light - Normal: green light On the details screen of a container or waybill When a waybill is "Due soon" or "Overdue", the system shows a matching ribbon as below. The system also provides the "Overdue" and "Due soon" filters and a grouping by "Overdue status" so you can filter the data easily:

sections.title: The dispatch status
sections.text: Dispatch status in the waybill list In the waybill list you can follow the dispatch status of the waybills through the information shown below: Field Description Task progress Shown as X / Y: - X is the number of tasks completed. - Y is the total number of tasks to carry out. Paired waybill The 20ft container waybill it is paired with. Dispatch order code The list of dispatch orders for that waybill. If there are several, each one is a separate row. Dispatch order status The state of the matching dispatch order. Carrier If the dispatch order is carried by a cooperative vehicle, it is shown here; otherwise three dashes - - - appear. Vehicle The licence plate for that dispatch order. If no vehicle has been assigned — the vehicle field is empty — three dashes - - - appear. Driver The driver's name for that dispatch order. If no driver has been assigned — the driver field is empty — three dashes - - - appear. Trailer The trailer's plate. If the waybill's task in that dispatch order has no trailer assigned — the trailer field is empty — three dashes - - - appear. Searching by dispatch status You can search containers and waybills by any of these fields: A few search tips - Type "---" and search by carrier to list the waybills carried by your own vehicles. - Type "---" and search by vehicle or driver to list the waybills that have a dispatch order but no vehicle or driver assigned to it yet.

sections.title: Filtering those that still need a vehicle
sections.text: The system provides the "Needs dispatch" filter: it lists the waybills that are confirmed but have no dispatch order yet, or have no dispatch order for all of their tasks.

sections.title: Driver task management menu
sections.text: The task management menus are: 1. Dispatcher tasks: contains the list of tasks for dispatchers.

sections.title: Creating a task
sections.text: The system separates tasks into two kinds - Tasks tied to a customer's container or waybill: - These are the tasks that get the waybill done, for example: pick up empty container, drop off empty container, pick up laden container, deliver laden container. - They have to be created from the container or waybill screen. - They also affect the driver's salary, because driver salary is calculated per waybill. - Tasks not tied to a customer's container or waybill: - These tasks do not belong to any container or waybill. The system still lets you assign a trailer and create a dispatch order for them so a driver can carry them out as usual. - Whether dispatchers use this depends on how they work. Creating a task for a container or waybill - Step 1: open a container or waybill → go to the [Tasks] tab. - Step 2: click Add a line to create a task for that container or waybill. The system shows a popup for the task details; fill in the Task information section as shown below. Field Description Task Select a task type, for example "Pick up empty container". Location Select where the task is carried out. Contact Enter the contact at that location, if any. Mobile Enter the contact's phone number. Note for the driver A note for the driver, if any. It is shown in the mobile app. Planned date Enter the date you plan the driver to carry out the task. The dispatcher sets a date that makes dispatching work well. Deadline Enter the deadline from the paperwork, or one the dispatcher sets to keep track of the task. Plan The container plan at the customer's warehouse. Applies to tasks such as "Deliver laden container" or "Drop off empty container" at a customer warehouse. The values are: drop container, detach trailer, store vehicle. This is also shown in the mobile app so the driver knows the plan. - Step 3: click SAVE & CLOSE if you only want one task, or SAVE & NEW to create another one. The task you added appears as below; you can reorder it so the sequence is right. - Step 4: click SAVE on the container or waybill, or press CTRL + S , to save. Once that is done the system generates a task code, as below: Creating a task not tied to a container or waybill - Step 1: go to one of the driver task management menus → click NEW to create a task. - Step 2: enter the task details, the same way as for a waybill task, and click SAVE to finish.

sections.title: Starting a task
sections.text: The system lets a dispatcher start a task. This is useful in a few situations: - Doing it on the driver's behalf: normally the driver starts the task in the mobile app. But sometimes the driver cannot use the app — for example they have lost their phone — and then the dispatcher can start the task for them. - Orders handed to a cooperative or an outside carrier: here the dispatcher keeps track of progress by phone or another channel and starts the task in the system. Steps Step 1 Open the task you want to start, either from a task management menu or from a dispatch order (1) → then click START (2). Step 2 The system asks whether you are sure you want to start the task. If you are, click OK. Step 3 The system shows a popup. Enter the actual start time — it defaults to now — and click OK . Result The system moves the task to the IN PROGRESS state.

sections.title: Completing a task
sections.text: The system lets a dispatcher complete a task. This is useful in a few situations: - Doing it on the driver's behalf: normally the driver completes the task in the mobile app. But sometimes the driver cannot use the app — for example they have lost their phone — and then the dispatcher can complete the task for them. - Orders handed to a cooperative or an outside carrier: here the dispatcher keeps track of progress by phone or another channel and completes the task in the system. Steps Step 1 Open the task you want to complete, either from a task management menu or by clicking the task on a dispatch order (1) → attach the related images and documents (2) on the task's [Documents] tab. Step 2 → Then click COMPLETE . Step 3 The system asks whether you are sure you want to complete the task. If you are, click OK. Step 4 The system shows a popup. Enter the actual completion time, and the container and seal numbers for the "pick up empty container" task of an export full container waybill, then click OK . Result: the system moves the task to the COMPLETED state:

sections.title: Reverting a task to not started
sections.text: Note The system lets you revert a task to the not started state when it is In progress, Completed or Cancelled. Reverting a task to not started Step 1 Open the task you want to revert → click REVERT TO NOT STARTED . Step 2 The system asks you to confirm. If you are sure, click OK. The system moves the task back to the NOT STARTED state:

sections.title: Canceling a task
sections.text: Note The system lets you cancel a task, but only while it is NOT STARTED . If you cancel every task of a container or waybill, that container or waybill also moves to the CANCELED state automatically. Canceling a task Step 1 Open the task you want to cancel → then click CANCEL . Step 2 The system asks you to confirm. If you are sure, click OK. The system moves the task to the CANCELED state:

sections.title: Deleting a task
sections.text: Note The system lets you delete a task, but only while it is NOT STARTED or CANCELED and the container or waybill has not been confirmed. Once the container or waybill is confirmed, you can only cancel the task. Deleting a task - Step 1: open a container or waybill → scroll down to the task list → select the task you want to delete (1) → click "Delete task" (2) → confirm in the popup. - Step 2 : open the task list in one of the task menus → tick the tasks you want to delete → click ACTIONS → click the delete action. - Step 3: the system asks you to confirm. If you are sure, click DELETE.

sections.title: The overdue status of a task
sections.text: The overdue status has three values 1. Overdue: past the deadline. 2. Due soon: within 6 hours of the deadline. 3. Normal: more than 6 hours before the deadline. In the task list The system shows a light column so you can tell the overdue status at a glance. - Overdue: red light - Due soon: yellow light - Normal: green light On the details screen of a task When a task is "Due soon" or "Overdue", the system shows a matching ribbon as below. The system also provides the "Overdue" and "Due soon" filters and a grouping by "Overdue status" so you can filter the data easily:

sections.title: Dispatch order management menu
sections.text: The dispatch order management menus are: Dispatch orders: this menu contains every dispatch order. Dispatch board: this menu contains the table that shows how dispatch orders are planned for each driver, so they are easier to manage. Driver timesheets: this menu contains the monthly timesheet of each driver. Incident history: this menu contains the list of dispatch orders in the "Incident" state.

sections.title: Creating a dispatch order
sections.text: Ways to create a dispatch order Option 1: from the "Container and waybill management" menu Follow the instructions in "Creating a dispatch order for a container or waybill" . Option 2: from the details screen of a container with no dispatch order yet Step 1: on the container details screen → click Dispatch → the dispatch order window opens. The image below shows the two task lists of the selected waybill or container: Two 20ft containers can share one dispatch order. You can choose which tasks to dispatch by ticking or unticking the Select column. The system ticks the tasks that have no vehicle yet by default. Tasks that already have a dispatch order still appear in this popup; for those, the Dispatch order column has a value. The [Vehicle & Driver] tab: fill this in when you want to create a new dispatch order for the tasks. Planned date : the system takes it from the planned date of the selected tasks. Driver : select the driver being assigned. Vehicle : when you select the driver, the system fills in that driver's default vehicle. You can still choose another one. Trailer : when you select the driver, the system fills in the default trailer for that driver's vehicle. You can still choose another one. Planned date : the system takes it from the planned date of the selected tasks. Note for the driver: a note for the dispatch order. Step 2: once everything is filled in, click CREATE or CREATE AND SEND TO DRIVER on the popup. If you choose to create the dispatch order: the system creates it and opens its screen. If you choose to create and send it to the driver: the system creates it, sends it to the driver, and opens its screen. Option 3: from the "Dispatch orders" menu Step 1: go to a Dispatch orders menu → click New . Step 2: select the vehicle and the driver you want to assign. Step 3: select the waybill to assign. Select the waybill you want from the waybill list. One dispatch order can take at most two waybills, for waybills with 20ft containers. For containers of 40ft or more, only one waybill fits in one dispatch order. Step 4: save the dispatch order with its assigned waybill. Step 5: the dispatch order is created. Once you save it, the system assigns the task list of the container or waybill to the order.

sections.title: Sending the order to the driver
sections.text: Once the dispatch order has been created with all its details, the dispatcher reviews everything on it and gets ready to send it to the driver. To send the order to the driver, click " Send to driver " on that dispatch order. Once confirmed, the dispatch order is sent through the mobile app to the driver assigned to it, and on the dispatcher screen the order moves to the " Confirmed " state.

sections.title: Accepting the order for the driver
sections.text: A dispatcher can accept (confirm) an order for the driver when the driver cannot use the app, or for an outside carrier. To confirm the order for the driver, click " Driver confirms " on that dispatch order. Once confirmed, the dispatch order changes state for the driver assigned to it in the mobile app, and on the dispatcher screen the order moves to the " Accepted by driver " state.

sections.title: Suspending a dispatch order (vehicle incident)
sections.text: If the driver is working on a dispatch order — the order is "In progress" — and something happens that stops them from continuing, the driver can call the dispatcher and ask them to report an "Incident". The dispatcher clicks "Incident" on the dispatch order, enters the reason and confirms. Once the dispatch order is moved to "Incident", its state changes to "Incident". The dispatcher can also resume the dispatch order by clicking "Resume trip". The dispatch order then moves back to "In progress" automatically.

sections.title: When a dispatch order is completed
sections.text: A dispatch order is completed when every task in it is completed, or when no task is left that is still pending or in progress. Once the driver or the dispatcher completes all the tasks in the dispatch order, its state moves to "Completed". In the dispatch order list, a completed order shows the "Completed" state in green, so the dispatcher can see the overall picture of every dispatch order at a glance.

sections.title: Splitting tasks out of a dispatch order
sections.text: There are two ways to split tasks out of a dispatch order: Case 1: Removing tasks from a dispatch order Step 1 The dispatcher selects the dispatch order with the tasks to remove. Step 2 Select the tasks to remove on the "Container & Tasks" tab. Only select tasks in the " Not started " state. Step 3 Click "Remove task" and confirm. Result: the system removes the tasks that have not started from that dispatch order. Those tasks still belong to the waybill, though, and still have to be completed. Case 2: Splitting some tasks out and assigning them to another order Step 1 The dispatcher selects the dispatch order with the tasks to split. Step 2 Select the tasks to split on the "Container & Tasks" tab. Only select tasks in the " Not started " state. Step 3 Click "Split order". Step 4 Assign an order to the tasks you selected: choose the date, the driver, and the vehicle and trailer. Step 5 Click the create button. "Create" makes a dispatch order in the "New" state; "Create & Send to driver" makes the order and sends it to the driver, in the "Awaiting confirmation" state. If you click "Create": the system creates a new dispatch order, does not send it to the driver, and opens its screen. If you click "Create and send to driver": the system creates a new dispatch order, sends it to the driver, and opens its screen. Result: the tasks have been split out of the dispatch order. The number of linked tasks drops by the number you split out, and those tasks are assigned to the dispatch order that was just created.

sections.title: Adding tasks to a dispatch order
sections.text: To add back tasks that were removed from a dispatch order, do the following: Step 1 The dispatcher selects the dispatch order to add the tasks to. Step 2 Click "Add task". The system shows a popup with the tasks of the waybill, in two groups: Tasks already in the order, which cannot be selected Tasks that can be added, which can be selected and are marked in orange Step 3 Select the tasks to add to the order (1) and click "Add task". Result: once you click the button, the selected tasks are added to the task list of that dispatch order.

sections.title: Deleting tasks from a dispatch order or waybill
sections.text: If the dispatcher wants to delete a task from the waybill entirely, do the following: Note: a deleted task is gone from the waybill completely. To get it back you have to add it again on the waybill. Step 1 The dispatcher selects the dispatch order with the tasks to delete: Step 2 Select the tasks to delete. Step 3 Click "Delete task", then click "OK" in the confirmation dialog. Result: the selected tasks have been deleted completely from both the order and the waybill.

sections.title: Delivery postponed before the driver starts
sections.text: For an "Import a full container" order where the driver has not started yet (the dispatch order is CONFIRMED or ACCEPTED BY DRIVER ) and the customer postpones the laden container delivery: - The dispatcher can adjust the planned time and the deadline of the task and keep the dispatch order as it is. - The dispatcher can adjust the planned time and the deadline of the task and at the same time reset the dispatch order to the new state — for example to dispatch a different driver.

sections.title: Hold laden container
sections.text: Example: An "Import a full container" order has these tasks: pick up laden container, deliver laden container, pick up empty container, return empty container. The driver has picked up the laden container but the customer postpones its delivery. The laden container now has to be stored at a depot and the tasks "Hold laden container" and "Pick up laden container" added to the dispatch order → the dispatcher can do this manually, or use this exception feature to save work. Steps Step 1 Open the dispatch order → click EXCEPTION . Step 2 The system shows the exception handling popup as below. - Select the situation and the reason: - Situation: the available situations are hold laden container, hold empty container and return empty container. - Reason: select the reason for the exception. - Select where the container is handled and the plan for dropping it: - Location: select where the container is stored. - Plan: select the storage plan. Here only the container is stored, so select "Drop container". If both the container and the trailer are stored, select "Detach trailer". If the container, the trailer and the vehicle are all stored, select "Store vehicle". - Applies to Container 1 / Container 2: select according to the number of containers on the waybill. If the dispatch order carries two 20ft containers, select both. Step 3 Once everything is filled in, the dispatcher clicks CONFIRM : The system adds the tasks "Hold laden container" and "Pick up laden container" into the middle of the laden container delivery of the current dispatch order, then returns to the previous dispatch order screen.

sections.title: Hold empty container
sections.text: Example: An "Export a full container" order has these tasks: pick up empty container, drop off empty container, pick up laden container, deliver laden container. The driver has picked up the empty container but the customer postpones its delivery. The empty container now has to be stored at a depot and the tasks "Hold empty container" and "Pick up empty container" added to the dispatch order → the dispatcher can do this manually, or use this exception feature to save work. Steps Step 1 Open the dispatch order → click EXCEPTION . Step 2 The system shows the exception handling popup as below. - Select the situation and the reason: - Situation: the available situations are hold laden container, hold empty container and return empty container. - Reason: select the reason for the exception. - Select where the container is handled and the plan for dropping it: - Location: select where the container is stored. - Plan: select the storage plan. Here only the container is stored, so select "Drop container". If both the container and the trailer are stored, select "Detach trailer". If the container, the trailer and the vehicle are all stored, select "Store vehicle". - Applies to Container 1 / Container 2: select according to the number of containers on the waybill. If the dispatch order carries two 20ft containers, select both. Step 3 Once everything is filled in, the dispatcher clicks CONFIRM : The system adds the tasks "Hold empty container" and "Pick up empty container" into the middle of the laden container delivery of the current dispatch order, then returns to the previous dispatch order screen.

sections.title: Return empty container
sections.text: Example: An "Export a full container" order has these tasks: pick up empty container, drop off empty container, pick up laden container, deliver laden container. The driver has picked up the empty container but the customer says it is not suitable. The empty container now has to be swapped at a depot and the tasks "Return empty container" and "Pick up empty container" added to the dispatch order → the dispatcher can do this manually, or use this exception feature to save work. Steps Step 1 Open the dispatch order → click EXCEPTION . Step 2 The system shows the exception handling popup as below. - Select the situation and the reason: - Situation: the available situations are hold laden container, hold empty container and return empty container. - Reason: select the reason for the exception. - Select where the container is handled and the plan for dropping it: - Location: select where the container is stored. - Plan: select the storage plan. Here only the container is stored, so select "Drop container". If both the container and the trailer are stored, select "Detach trailer". If the container, the trailer and the vehicle are all stored, select "Store vehicle". - Applies to Container 1 / Container 2: select according to the number of containers on the waybill. If the dispatch order carries two 20ft containers, select both. Step 3 Once everything is filled in, the dispatcher clicks CONFIRM : The system adds the tasks "Return empty container" and "Pick up empty container" into the middle of the laden container delivery of the current dispatch order, then returns to the previous dispatch order screen.

sections.title: Driver board management menu
sections.text: To view and manage the boards shown in the Mobile App, do the following: On the main menu bar, select Fleet Driver boards. The system shows the list of driver boards.

sections.title: Creating a driver board
sections.text: Steps Step 1 Go to the Driver boards menu and click the create button. Step 2 Enter the information: - Title: enter the name of the notice (this name is not shown in the mobile app). - Description: enter the content of the board (this part is shown in the mobile app). - You can use some basic formatting for the notice content: Step 3 Click the save button to finish creating the board. Note: a newly created board is only in the DRAFT state. You have to confirm it before it appears in the mobile app for drivers.

sections.title: Confirming a driver board
sections.text: Steps Step 1 On a board in the DRAFT state, click CONFIRM : The board moves to the CONFIRMED state. Only then does it appear in the mobile app for drivers.

sections.title: Sorting driver boards
sections.text: Back on the board list, you can drag and drop the boards to change their order. Move the mouse pointer to the drag handle of a board. Hold the handle down, drag the board to the position you want, then release the mouse to reorder it. This order is the order in which the boards appear in the Mobile App.

sections.title: Driver leave management menu
sections.text: Accessing the leave list Screen: Partners Driver leave Access rights: Master Data User Use the path above to open the screen where you view driver leave. On the driver leave list screen you can view the leave records of drivers. Viewing leave on a monthly calendar Click to switch to the monthly calendar view and see the drivers' leave.

sections.title: Creating driver leave (for dispatchers)
sections.text: Note The driver mobile app already lets drivers request leave themselves. Once a driver submits a request, it is pushed to the system in the NEW state. If for any reason a dispatcher needs to create leave on a driver's behalf, they can do it as described below. Steps Step 1 Go to the Leave menu and click the create button. Step 2 Enter the following information: - Reason: Required. Enter the reason for the leave. - Description: enter a description. - Driver: select the driver. When you open this from a driver record, the system fills in the driver automatically. - Dates: Required. Select the leave date range. Step 3 Click the save button to finish creating the leave record. A newly created record is in the NEW state. The system calculates the following three values automatically to give the dispatcher more context: - Hours off: the system calculates the number of hours off from the selected date range. - Days off: the system calculates the number of days off from the selected date range. - Approved days this month: the system totals the days of leave already approved for this driver in the current month. The system highlights the figure in red when the approved days for the month reach or exceed the allowance (currently 4 days per month). Starting from a driver record You can also start creating leave from the Partners Drivers screen. Step 1 On the driver list, select the driver you want to create leave for. Step 2 On the driver form view, click DRIVER LEAVE to open the driver's leave management list. Step 3 On the driver leave management list, click NEW to create a new leave record, then enter the information described above and click SAVE .

sections.title: Approving, rejecting or canceling driver leave
sections.text: To approve a driver's leave: on a record in the new state → click APPROVE . To reject a driver's leave: on a record in the new state → click REJECT . To cancel a driver's leave: on the record → click CANCEL . You can also approve, reject or cancel several records at once:

sections.title: Configuring cost groups
sections.text: Steps Step 1 Go to the Cost groups menu and click the create button. Step 2 Enter the information: - Cost group: enter the name of the cost group. - Parent category: select the parent group, if any.

sections.title: Configuring cost types
sections.text: Steps Step 1 Go to the Cost types menu and click the create button. Step 2 Enter the basic information: - Cost type: enter the name of the cost. - Cost group: select the cost group. - Internal code: enter the cost code. - Tax: select the VAT type. When this cost type is recorded, the system calculates the default tax amount from the tax type configured here. Step 3 Open the [Cost configuration] tab to add some more advanced settings: - Needs approval: tick this if a dispatcher has to approve the cost after a driver creates it. - Driver required: tick this to manage the cost type per driver. When a cost is created, the system requires the driver who incurred it. - Dispatch order required: tick this to manage the cost type per dispatch order. When a cost is created, the system requires the dispatch order it belongs to. - Vehicle required: tick this to manage the cost type per vehicle. When a cost is created, the system requires the vehicle that incurred it. - Invoice or document required: tick this if an invoice or document must be attached to the cost. - Location required: tick this to manage the cost type per location. When a cost is created, the system requires the location where it was incurred. - Show in the mobile app: tick this if you want the cost type to appear in the Mobile App, so drivers can create it. If you leave it unticked, only dispatchers can create this type of cost. - Note for the driver: this note appears in the driver mobile app when the driver records this type of cost.

sections.title: Cost management menu
sections.text: - All costs: this menu collects every cost record by dispatch order. - Waybill costs: this menu shows the costs allocated to each container (waybill).

sections.title: Creating a cost (for dispatchers)
sections.text: Note The driver mobile app already lets drivers record their additional costs and upload the invoices and documents. Use this function when a dispatcher needs to create the cost themselves. Steps Step 1 Go to the All costs menu and click the create button. Step 2 Enter the information: - Cost date: select the date the cost was incurred. - Cost type: select the type of cost. - Amount: enter the amount, including tax. - Tax: select the tax type, if any. - Description: enter a description of the cost, if any. - Invoice / Document: attach the invoice or document. - Driver: select the driver. - Dispatch order: select the dispatch order the cost belongs to, if required. - Vehicle: select the vehicle that incurred the cost, if required. - Location: select the location where the cost was incurred, if required. - Some additional information: - Supplier: select the service supplier, if that supplier already exists in the system. - Invoice number: enter the invoice number. - Serial number: enter the invoice serial number. - Tax code: enter the tax code of the service supplier. Step 3 Click the save button to finish creating the cost record. A newly created record is in the NEW state. Step 4 Click CONFIRM to confirm the cost record. - If the cost type is configured to need approval, the record moves to WAITING FOR APPROVAL after you confirm it. - If the cost type is not configured to need approval, the record moves straight to APPROVED after you confirm it.

sections.title: Approving a cost
sections.text: Steps Step 1 Open a cost record in the WAITING FOR APPROVAL state and click APPROVE . The cost record moves to the APPROVED state. You can also approve several cost records at once: on the cost list, select the records you want to approve and click APPROVE as shown below.

sections.title: Rejecting a cost
sections.text: Steps Step 1 Open a cost record in the WAITING FOR APPROVAL state and click REJECT . The cost record moves to the REJECTED state.

sections.title: Marking the payment or reimbursement status
sections.text: Payment and reimbursement statuses There are four payment and reimbursement statuses: - Not processed: the payment or reimbursement to the driver has not been processed. - In progress: the payment or reimbursement to the driver is being processed. - Paid in full: the driver has been paid or reimbursed the full amount. - Partially paid: the driver has been paid or reimbursed part of the amount. Marking In progress On an APPROVED cost record, click MOVE TO IN PROGRESS . Marking Paid in full On an APPROVED cost record, click MOVE TO PAID IN FULL . Marking Partially paid On an APPROVED cost record, enter the amount already paid and click save. The system moves the record to the PARTIALLY PAID status automatically.
